confirmed_findings.finding: MSF05 controlling normalized RN iff mentions arbitrary dominating P0 without requiring it share the models conditional law. This is false as written.

Actual common-reference Statement explicitly fixes theta0 in nonempty Theta and P0=P_theta0. Its marginal-RN disintegration argument correctly uses sufficiency under P0; reverse direction only needs a reference RCD and T-measurable derivatives. Existing source does not claim the false arbitrary-reference necessity.

Existing standard-Borel dominated factorization theorem covers arbitrary sigma-finite base mu and uncountable nonempty model, with canonical common h=dQ/dmu for a dominating countable model mixture Q. Augmenting the family by Q is legitimate because its kernel identity follows by countable mixing; no assumption Q is an original model member is imposed.

counterexample_checked.verification: Common kernel K(t,.)=delta_(t,0) proves sufficiency. R gives every atom positive mass; densities4theta or4(1-theta) at u=0 but zero at u=1 are not constant on T-fibers, and no R-null alteration can fix. Parameter interval stays nonsymmetric/general; do not replace with symmetric finite models.
counterexample_checked.full_factorization_still_true: Relative to external R take common h=2*1{u=0}, a density of Q=(P_1/4+P_3/4)/2; g_theta(1)=2theta,g_theta(0)=2(1-theta). Then dP_theta/dR=h*g_theta(T). This explicitly separates false normalized criterion from true external common-h factorization.

independent_proof_checks: For member P0, common kernel K disintegrates Ptheta and P0. Since Ptheta^T<<P0^T, r=dPtheta^T/dP0^T yields Ptheta(A)=integral K(y,A)r(y)dP0^T=integral_A r(T)dP0 by simple-function/monotone extension of disintegration. RN uniqueness proves T-measurable ratio.

For any reference R with T-measurable ratio gtheta(T), its RCD K_R reweights to a common conditional kernel under all Ptheta. Thus only forward necessity fails for arbitrary reference; do not incorrectly deny the sufficient direction.

Countable domination uses finite equivalent lambda, support finite-union supremum and countably approximating supports. Any omitted support positive outside maximal union increases its finite-union supremum, contradiction; positive mixture then dominates every model law.

Common kernel under selected model laws extends to their positive countable mixture by nonnegative integral sum. Augment by Q to use member-reference criterion, then multiply RN densities by h=dQ/dmu. Reverse ptheta=h*gtheta(T) relative to this fixed Q gives dPtheta/dQ=gtheta(T) on {h>0}, a Q-full set; add derivative1 for Q and apply same criterion. This maintains arbitrary sigma-finite external base.

For more general factorization with an arbitrary common h0, q(T)=sum_j w_j g_theta_j(T), dQ/dmu=h0*q(T). On Q-full positive q(T), normalized ratios gtheta(T)/q(T) give the same reverse conditional-kernel argument. Standard full Fisher–Neyman scope therefore remains valid.

proposed_plan_edit.exact_before_clause: `thm-common-reference-factorization-criterion` (assume AC for the RCD/Doob–Dynkin clauses): for a standard-Borel data/statistic space and reference probability $P_0$ with every $P_\theta\ll P_0$, sufficiency iff each $dP_\theta/dP_0$ is $\sigma(T)$-measurable $P_0$-a.e., equivalently $q_\theta\circ T$ by Doob–Dynkin; prove by writing the conditional law from a reference RCD and the marginal RN derivative.
proposed_plan_edit.exact_after_clause: `thm-common-reference-factorization-criterion` (assume AC for the RCD/Doob–Dynkin clauses): for standard-Borel data/statistic spaces, a nonempty model, and an in-model reference probability $P_0=P_{\theta_0}$ with every $P_\theta\ll P_0$, sufficiency iff each $dP_\theta/dP_0$ has a $\sigma(T)$-measurable version $P_0$-a.e., equivalently $q_\theta\circ T$ by Doob–Dynkin; prove by writing the shared conditional law under the in-model reference and the marginal RN derivative. An arbitrary external dominating law need not share that conditional law and does not give this normalized iff; retain the full external-dominator Fisher–Neyman common-$h$ factorization in `thm-standard-borel-dominated-factorization-criterion` below, using a dominating countable mixture and the augmented family.
proposed_plan_edit.exact_before_row: | **MSF-05** `complete-sufficiency-exponential-families-and-basu` — Sufficiency, Completeness and Exponential Families | MSF-04; MSF-02; `conditional-distributions-and-regular-conditional-probability`; `conditional-expectation`; `probability/standard-borel-real-codings-and-determining-classes`; `probability/infinite-product-measures-and-kolmogorov-extension`; `topology/complete-metrizability-and-baire`; `functional-analysis/fourier-transform-convolution-and-approximate-identities`; `complex-analysis/the-identity-theorem-and-the-open-mapping-theorem` | `def-sufficient-statistic`: for standard-Borel data and statistic spaces, a supplied regular conditional law of data given $T$ is parameter-independent; `def-minimal-sufficient-sigma-field`: a sufficient $\mathcal G$ is minimal if it is contained, modulo the common null ideal $\{N:P_\theta(N)=0\text{ for all }\theta\}$, in every sufficient sigma-field; for a countable dominated family with positive-mixture reference $Q$, this means inclusion modulo $Q$-null sets. `def-minimal-sufficient-statistic`: a standard-Borel statistic whose generated sigma-field is minimal modulo the family-null ideal; a single measurable factor map from every other sufficient statistic is asserted only in the countable dominated case with positive-mixture reference $Q$, where factorization holds $Q$-a.s. (hence $P_k$-a.s. for every $k$). No pointwise/common factor-map claim is made for an arbitrary uncountable family. `thm-countable-factorization-criterion-for-sufficiency`: on a countable sample space, $T$ is sufficient iff $p_\theta(x)=g_\theta(Tx)h(x)$ with the zero-fiber convention stated. `def-likelihood-ratio-equivalence-on-common-discrete-support`: on a countable sample space with common support $\mathcal X_0$ satisfying $P_\theta(\mathcal X_0)=1$ and $p_\theta(x)>0$ for every $x\in\mathcal X_0$ and $\theta$, set $x\sim y$ iff $p_\theta(x)/p_\theta(y)$ is constant in $\theta$. `thm-discrete-likelihood-ratio-classes-are-minimal-sufficient`: if $T(x)=T(y)$ exactly when $x\sim y$ on $\mathcal X_0$, then $T$ is minimal sufficient modulo the family-null set $\mathcal X\setminus\mathcal X_0$. Proof: the conditional mass $P_\theta(X=x\mid T=t)=1/\sum_{z:T(z)=t}p_\theta(z)/p_\theta(x)$ is parameter-free, and any sufficient $S$ only merges likelihood-ratio-equivalent points, so $T$ factors through $S$. This is the fully read Fithian discrete proof, with common support explicit. `thm-common-reference-factorization-criterion` (assume AC for the RCD/Doob–Dynkin clauses): for a standard-Borel data/statistic space and reference probability $P_0$ with every $P_\theta\ll P_0$, sufficiency iff each $dP_\theta/dP_0$ is $\sigma(T)$-measurable $P_0$-a.e., equivalently $q_\theta\circ T$ by Doob–Dynkin; prove by writing the conditional law from a reference RCD and the marginal RN derivative. `thm-countable-mixture-dominates-sigmafinite-dominated-family` (Halmos–Savage type; assume AC): for a nonempty family of probabilities dominated by a sigma-finite $\mu$, construct a finite probability $\lambda\sim\mu$ by weighting a finite-measure exhaustion; take finite unions of supports $\{p_\theta>0\}$ approaching the supremum of their $\lambda$-masses; their countable union contains every support modulo $\lambda$; a positive-weight countable mixture $Q$ of the selected $P_\theta$ then dominates the whole family. Prove the support-maximization step by adjoining any omitted support and contradicting the supremum. `thm-countable-mixture-likelihood-ratio-vector-is-minimal-sufficient`: for a countable model $(P_k)_{k\ge1}$ on a standard-Borel sample space, choose $w_k>0$, $\sum_kw_k=1$, and the positive mixture $Q=\sum_kw_kP_k$. Choose Borel versions $f_k=dP_k/dQ$, modifying them on one common $Q$-null set to be finite, and set $T(x)=(f_k(x))_{k\ge1}\in[0,\infty)^\mathbb N$, a standard-Borel target. Each $f_k$ is a coordinate of $T$, so the conditional-density/RCD supplier makes the conditional law parameter-free and $T$ sufficient. For any standard-Borel sufficient $S$, $Q$ inherits its common conditional kernel by mixture and $f_k=E_Q[f_k\mid\sigma(S)]$ $Q$-a.s.; countability gives one common full-$Q$ set on which every coordinate is $S$-measurable. Standard-Borel real coding and Doob–Dynkin then give $T=\varphi(S)$ $Q$-a.s., proving minimality. This is a countable-model proof. `thm-standard-borel-dominated-factorization-criterion` (local proof obligation): for a standard-Borel sample space, measurable statistic into a standard-Borel space, nonempty family of probabilities dominated by sigma-finite $\mu$, and supplied common everywhere probability-kernel version of sufficiency, $T$ is sufficient iff there exist probability density $h=dQ/d\mu$ for a countable mixture $Q$ that dominates the family and nonnegative measurable $g_\theta$ such that $p_\theta(x)=h(x)g_\theta(Tx)$ $\mu$-a.e. for each $\theta$ (exceptional null sets may depend on $\theta$). Proof route: use the countable-mixture supplier; its conditional kernel remains common by countable mixing. If $T$ is sufficient, then $dP_\theta/dQ=E_Q[dP_\theta/dQ\mid\sigma(T)]$ $Q$-a.s.; factor through $T$ by Doob–Dynkin and multiply by $h$. Conversely the density factorization gives $dP_\theta/dQ=g_\theta(T)/\sum_k w_kg_k(T)$ on fibers with positive mixture density, hence this RN derivative is $\sigma(T)$-measurable; change of measure preserves the common RCD under every $P_\theta$, with arbitrary probability fillers only on a common $Q$-null set. Do not claim the product-density conditional formula applies to the singular graph law $(X,T(X))$. The local proof must verify countable-support selection, denominator-zero fibers, countable determining classes, and the per-parameter a.e. equalities. `def-complete-statistic`: $E_\theta g(T)=0$ for every $\theta$ implies $g(T)=0$ a.s.; `def-ancillary-statistic`: the statistic's law is independent of $\theta$; `def-exponential-family`: on a specified sigma-finite base measure $\mu$, a dominated family has density $p_\eta(x)=h(x)\exp\{\eta\cdot S(x)-A(\eta)\}$ where $h,S$ are measurable, $A(\eta)=\log\int h(x)e^{\eta\cdot S(x)}d\mu(x)<\infty$ on the natural-parameter set, and the family is normalized there; `thm-full-rank-exponential-family-sufficiency`: $S$ is sufficient by the common-reference criterion; `lem-uniqueness-of-a-multivariate-exponential-transform`: if a finite signed measure has an exponential moment on an open neighborhood and its Laplace transform vanishes there, it is zero; prove holomorphy in a product strip by exponential domination, coordinatewise identity continuation and existing finite-measure Fourier uniqueness; `thm-completeness-of-full-exponential-family`: under AC, a full-rank family whose natural-parameter set contains an open subset of $\mathbb R^k$, and integrability of $g(S)$ under each parameter, $E_\eta g(S)=0$ throughout that set implies $g(S)=0$ a.s.; reduce to transform uniqueness with all exponential-integrability assumptions checked; `thm-basu-independence`: under AC, complete sufficiency implies independence from every ancillary statistic. B: Bernoulli count as a minimal sufficient statistic, the countable likelihood-ratio vector, normal sample mean/residual, a curved/non-open family where completeness fails, and a dominated family illustrating the countable-mixture reference. | F01 complete. Martin §2.3 pp.33–40; Tebbs §9.3 pp.118–131; MIT 18.655 Note 6 pp.4–10, 17–20; Fithian “Sufficiency” lines 42–340 and “Completeness, Ancillarity, and Basu’s Theorem” lines 42–177; Geyer §8 pp.17–18. The dossier supports discrete minimality and countable/common-reference sufficiency criteria, but found no complete source proof of unrestricted dominated factorization/minimality. This row gives a local dominated-factorization route with an explicit countable-mixture denominator; its full proof remains a draft obligation. |
